thread:
maya: Heads-up — we had two OOM spikes on prod-hosts this morning correlated with a KV cache surge after the new long-context rollout. Observed GPU mem hit ~98% before crash.
liam: Oh no. Any quick numbers on hit-rate / item counts? Was eviction happening?
maya: Cache hit-rate dropped from 87% to 62% over ~10m as many new prefixes got inserted. Evictions were happening but LRU churn looked high. Fragmentation metric spiked.
ryan: Do we have profiling traces from the runtime? kernel selection stats + batching counts during the window?
maya: Pushed profiling dump to /shared/perf/dumps/1746801234.zip. Key snippets:

perf-bot: <automated summary> 10:03-10:13: sustained high allocation churn, many small allocations from KV cache; GPU mem pressure triggered async flushes.

anika: Quick config we ran previously for TTLs:
```
kv_cache:
  max_entries_gpu: 1_000_000
  max_bytes_gpu: 12GB
  eviction_policy: LRU
  default_ttl_s: 3600
  per_model_ttl: { 'long-context-v2': 7200 }
```

liam: Looks like default_ttl allowed stale prefixes to accumulate; long-context-v2 per-model ttl might be too high for tail workloads.
ryan: From the profiling: kernel selection shifted to smaller GEMM kernels due to sequence-length variability, increasing memory temp buffers. Combined with caching many small KV shards -> fragmentation.

maya: Proposed mitigations:
- lower per-model TTL for long-context-v2 to 600s
- enable prefix warmup async policy to pre-allocate shared KV slabs
- add approximation of item size to bias eviction (size-aware LRU)

anika: Size-aware eviction would help — current LRU treats all entries equal. We could implement a cost function = entry_bytes * recency_factor.

liam: Quick A/B? Reduce TTL in staging and run 6-hour soak with synthetic tail workload. Also patch to report avg_entry_size in telemetry.

maya: I've already deployed TTL tweak to staging: per-model ttl -> 600s, enabled finer-grained eviction logging.

ryan: Two more notes:
1) Batching heuristics bump: during the surge batching window shrank to 1 because latency controller prioritized tail latency; we should allow controlled batching under mem pressure.
2) Kernel selection: add a guard to prefer kernels with lower transient buffer footprint when fragmentation > 0.6.

anika: Agreed. Also add a periodic compaction pass on CPU-side KV to defragment (cheap background job). Could be off by default and enabled on high-frag signals.

sophia: (ops) If we change TTLs we need a coordinated rollout and a migration plan for Dedicated customers — doc note?
liam: I'll add runbook: how to adjust max_entries/max_bytes, TTL, and how to drain caches safely.

maya: Action items:
- liam: run staging soak with new TTL + telemetry for avg_entry_size (ETA: 2h)
- ryan: prototype kernel-selection guard and compaction flag (ETA: EOD)
- anika: size-aware eviction sketch + perf test (ETA: 2 days)
- sophia: update runbook and customer notif draft (ETA: tomorrow)

liam: I'll post soak results in this thread when done. Thanks all :thumbsup:
